discovery: Photonic crystals and the photonic band gap: inhibition of spontaneous emission and localization of light
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently proposed that periodic dielectric structures could create a photonic band gap, a frequency range in which no electromagnetic modes exist. Yablonovitch showed this would inhibit spontaneous emission; John showed it enables strong localization of light and new emitter-photon bound states. Yablonovitch then fabricated the first three-dimensional photonic band gap crystal ('Yablonovite'). The concept created an entirely new field: photonic-crystal cavities with ultrahigh quality factors and tiny mode volumes made solid-state cavity quantum electrodynamics possible, including strong coupling and single-photon nonlinearities with individual quantum dots and colour centres. Photonic-crystal fibres, slow-light devices, photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers and today's integrated quantum photonic circuits all rest on these ideas. Few concepts have so fundamentally changed how we control light-matter interaction, from basic quantum optics to industrial technology.
